title: Platform systems & services: playbook, dashboards, runbooks, and roadmap
author: Sofia Martinez
content:
Overview

This playbook consolidates the Platform Engineering team's canonical guidance for systems and services across the Redwood Inference platform: operational runbooks, dashboard and alert ownership, common how-tos, retrospective learnings, and the near-term roadmap. The goal is a single source of truth for SLO, alert, and runbook changes that impact hosted, dedicated, and private deployments.

Scope
- Applies to platform-managed services running in the Redwood control plane and the dedicated management plane (k8s control plane, Redis caches, metrics stack, ingress/proxy).
- Excludes customer-managed application stacks; see eng-private-deployments for on-prem integration guides.

Owners & RACI
- Primary owner: Platform Systems & Services (eng-platform).
- SRE oncall: first responder for platform-facing incidents.
- Service owner: each service listed below retains code and config ownership.
- RACI summary:
  1. Service outage: SRE (R), Service Owner (A), Platform Eng (C), Customer Success (I)
  2. Dashboard or alert change: Service Owner (R), Platform Eng (A), SRE (C)
  3. Roadmap feature affecting infra: Product (R), Platform Eng (A), Security (C)

Key services covered
- feed-proxy (edge ingress + routing) — owner: traffic-service-team, deployed to k8s-cluster-prod, exposes /v1/generate
- model-router (model selection + variant routing) — owner: serving-runtime-team, runs on dedicated GPU pools
- kv-cache (Redis 6.2 cluster) — owner: platform-storage, used for prefix/KV caching and rate limiting
- metrics-stack (Prometheus + Cortex + Grafana) — owner: observability-team
- job-runner (batch/async inference jobs) — owner: batch-services

SLOs and error budget policy
- Latency SLOs (p99):
  - feed-proxy (edge routing): 120 ms p99 for 95% of traffic (measured at ingress-to-backend handoff)
  - model-router: 200 ms p99 for local routing decisions
  - kv-cache GET: 10 ms p99
- Availability SLOs (monthly uptime): 99.95% for control plane services; 99.9% for non-critical batch components
- Error budget burn policy: any service consuming >25% of monthly error budget must create a mitigation plan within 48 hours and schedule a postmortem if >50% burn in 7 days.

Dashboards & alerting standards
- All dashboards are in Grafana and follow the common dashboard template: Overview, Capacity, Latency & Errors, Recent Deploys, and Runbook link.
- Naming convention: [service-name] / [environment] / [dashboard-type] (e.g., model-router / prod / overview).
- Alert naming convention: alert_[service]_[severity]_[metric] (e.g., alert_model-router_p1_request-error-rate).

Required dashboards (table)
| Dashboard name | Owner | Key metrics | Refresh | Runbook |
|---------------|-------|-------------|---------|--------|
| feed-proxy / prod / overview | traffic-service-team | 5xx rate, p95/p99 latency, QPS | 15s | feed-proxy-runbook |
| model-router / prod / overview | serving-runtime-team | model-variant-fallbacks, routing-latency, CPU/GPU util | 15s | model-router-runbook |
| kv-cache / prod / capacity | platform-storage | hit-rate, evictions, memory-usage | 30s | kv-cache-runbook |

Alert thresholds (examples)
- P1: service error rate > 1% (5m window) AND traffic > 10rps — page SRE oncall immediately.
- P1: control plane CPU > 90% sustained for 5m — trigger autoscaling and page SRE.
- P2: cache hit-rate < 70% for 10m — notify service owner via Slack channel #platform-alerts.
- P3: dashboard missing panels or datasource errors — file a Jira ticket assigned to observability-team.

Runbooks (quick-reference)
- Standard runbook structure (must be present in each service runbook):
  1. Symptom and impact
  2. Immediate mitigation steps (0–15m)
  3. Intermediate steps (15–60m)
  4. Root-cause investigation checklist
  5. Restoration & rollback procedures
  6. Postmortem owner and timeline

Example: feed-proxy P1 (high 5xx rate)
1) Confirm: check feed-proxy / prod / overview for 5xx spike, correlated deploys, and backend latency.
2) Immediate mitigation:
   a) Roll back last prod deploy if deploy time correlates with spike (kubectl rollout undo deployment/feed-proxy -n prod).
   b) Temporarily scale replicas: kubectl scale deployment/feed-proxy --replicas=8 -n prod (note: this may increase load on backends).
   c) Enable 429-based rate limiting fallback: POST /admin/ratelimit/enable on control endpoint.
3) Intermediate: divert 10% traffic to model-variant-fallback (traffic-split rule) and monitor error rate.
4) Investigate: collect logs (centralized ELK): curl 'https://elk.internal/_search?q=feed-proxy%20error' or use Kibana query feed-proxy-5xx.
5) Restore: once 5xx < 0.1% for 10m, gradually revert traffic split and scale down replicas.
6) Postmortem: owner schedules postmortem within 72 hours; link to postmortem template (postmortem-template).

Escalation & communication
- Pager duty → Slack escalation: page SRE oncall (P1) → if not acknowledged in 5m, escalate to platform lead.
- Customer-facing comms: Customer Success drafts status updates using the incident-status template; platform lead provides technical summary.

Common how-tos (examples)
- Adding a new Grafana panel:
  1. Create the panel in dev Grafana, verify queries and time ranges.
  2. Add panel metadata: owner, runbook link, alert rules if appropriate.
  3. Submit for review in #observability-review with screenshot and queries.
  4. After approval, apply to prod dashboard using grafana-cli dashboard import --file <json>.
- Updating an alert threshold:
  1. Propose change in Jira with justification (customer impact, false positives, capacity change).
  2. Run alert simulation against 30 days of metrics using alert-tooling.sh --simulate.
  3. If results are acceptable, merge change and notify SRE and service owner.

Roadmap (next three quarters)
- Q1 2026:
  - Rollout unified dashboard templates for Dedicated clusters (milestone: all dedicated clusters adopt template by 2026-03-31).
  - Add golden signals collection at service-level (trace + metrics correlation).
- Q2 2026:
  - Implement dynamic alert tuning using historical baseline models to reduce noise by 30%.
  - Introduce runbook automation for common mitigations (auto-rollbacks for deploy-correlated spikes).
- Q3 2026:
  - Expand capacity observability for GPU pools with per-tenant chargeback metrics.
  - Provide an on-prem observability bundle for Private deployments.

Recent retrospective (summary)
- Incident: 2025-09-14 feed-proxy spike (postmortem link internal/postmortem-2025-09-14) highlighted: inadequate canary coverage and noisy cache eviction alerts. Actions completed:
  - Canary rollout policy updated to 5% -> 25% staged rollouts with automated health checks.
  - Cache alert thresholds revised; added ephemerality decay filter to reduce false positives.

Appendix: useful commands and links
- Grafana: https://grafana.internal (read-only for non-observability members).
- Kibana/ELK: https://elk.internal
- Alert simulation tool: gitlab.com/redwood/observability/alert-tooling.sh
- Common kubectl aliases:
  - alias k=kubectl
  - k get pods -n prod -l app=feed-proxy

Checklist for any config change
1. Update dashboard and runbook before making infra changes.
2. Add an entry to the change-log (Confluence change template).
3. Notify #platform-announcements and the service owner 48 hours prior for any P1-impacting change.

Contact & next steps
- For questions about this playbook or to request exceptions, file a Jira ticket assigned to team:eng-platform-playbooks.
- Next scheduled review: 2026-04-15 (quarterly cadence).
